title: Health Outcomes of CAPABLE in Permanent Supportive Housing
official: Health Outcomes of CAPABLE in Permanent Supportive Housing
summary:
This study will evaluate whether Community Aging in Place-Advancing Better Living for Elders (CAPABLE) improves daily functioning among adults aged 45 years and older who live in permanent supportive housing and have difficulty performing everyday activities.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either CAPABLE in addition to their usual services or usual services alone. CAPABLE is a person-directed, home-based program delivered by an occupational therapist and a registered nurse. Participants assigned to CAPABLE may receive up to 10 home visits over approximately six months, including up to six occupational therapy visits and four nursing visits. Assistive devices and minor home modifications may also be provided based on each participant's goals and needs.

The study will enroll approximately 634 participants in Los Angeles County. Researchers will assess participants at enrollment and at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. The main outcomes are participants' ability to perform activities of daily living and instrumental activities of daily living. The study will also examine health-related quality of life, health care use, housing stability, and the cost-effectiveness of CAPABLE.

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Able and willing to provide informed consent
* Client of the Los Angeles County Department of Health Services
* Living in permanent supportive housing
* Age 45 years or older
* Cognitively intact or experiencing only mild cognitive impairment
* Proficient in English or Spanish
* Reports some or a lot of difficulty performing at least one activity of daily living or instrumental activity of daily living

Exclusion Criteria:

* Does not meet one or more inclusion criteria
* Unwilling or unable to provide informed consent
* Withdraws consent
